For Percutaneous Ethanol Injection (PEI) for Benign Cystic Thyroid Nodules, the preferred approach seems to be percutaneous ethanol injection without aspiration of ethanol-mixed fluid. This method can provide effective treatment with minimal invasiveness and lower risk compared to aspiration.

Aspiration of ethanol-mixed fluid may have benefits in certain scenarios but is not generally recommended as a standard practice for PEI. The question highlights the importance of understanding that while FS (fine-needle aspiration) was once used, its role has changed due to various factors including time required, cost associated with it, and potential drawbacks.

Given these considerations, it appears that percutaneous ethanol injection without aspiration of ethanol-mixed fluid is currently considered the most advantageous approach for treating benign cystic thyroid nodules.
